reasons: Both answers meet every rubric item with nearly identical designs: a refactor to an injectable client, httpx.MockTransport unit tests, clamping to 50, readable 400 errors, and an opt-in contract test. B has an internal inconsistency: it switches to r.json().get("items", []), so a renamed items key would silently return an empty list, and its contract test explicitly accepts empty results, even though B says that test exists to catch exactly that rename. A keeps the strict key access and rejects a non-positive limit explicitly instead of silently coercing it to 1, which gives it a slight edge, although B does include runnable code for the contract test's 400 check.

B: Claims the contract test catches 'items' being renamed, but .get("items", []) plus accepting empty results means it would not
